Every wiki claim above is one the page states in prose or in a table; none is inferred from an image nobody looked at. This is why the file records what a roster CONTAINS and in what ORDER, and never how it is laid out.

The Arcane Odyssey page carries the wiki's own 'Needs Info' and 'Future Content' category tags, so its five-rank permission ladder is weaker evidence than Deepwoken's published matrix or BedWars' four-rank description. It is kept because the rank-names-are-editable and honorific-Elite observations are specific enough to check, and it is flagged rather than dropped.

The Blox Fruits crew page contradicts itself about its leaderboard — 'top 99 crews' in one line and 'will only show 100 crews' in the next — and its kick instructions tell the player to click the Invite button. Both are recorded as written rather than silently corrected, because the wiki is the source and guessing which way it is wrong would be inventing.

The LaunchData bug report's last post is 2025-12-12, a developer describing the failure as intermittent and sometimes cleared by restarting the client; the last Roblox Staff post before it, 2025-11-03, asks for a reproduction after failing to hit the bug in a test experience. WHETHER IT IS FIXED NOW IS UNKNOWN and nothing in the thread says it is. The rule above is written to be safe either way — a screen that degrades gracefully when LaunchData is blank costs nothing if the bug is gone. FOR THE NEXT READER, AND IT APPLIES TO EVERY DEVFORUM ROW IN THIS FILE RATHER THAN ONLY THIS ONE: a topic's default .json stream returns about twenty posts, not the topic. Here it stops at post 21 and silently omits post 22, and only the payload's own last_posted_at showed that a later post existed — which is exactly how the 2025-11-03 date got into this row. The other two DevForum rows were read through the same window and, until the third pass, did not say so; both now declare it in their source lines. t/4644214 returns 20 posts ending at post 25 against posts_count 45 / highest_post_number 52 / last_posted_at 2026-08-27, and t/4513813 returns 20 ending at post 20 against posts_count 330 / highest 347 / last 2026-08-11. No claim in either row was falsified — all of them sit in post 1 and posts 2–5, re-read verbatim on 2026-09-20 — but a partial window has to be declared, not discovered.

One claim in the BedWars chat row is the wiki's own speculation and is marked as such in the row: that /hub was replaced by /lobby because of Roblox warnings. It is recorded because the rename itself is checkable; the motive is not.

No source read here describes what a social screen does when it is EMPTY — no friends online, a guild with one member, an invite list with nobody in it. The friends-list row records that a count of online friends is shown, which is the closest anything comes. Empty states on this screen are unbacked.

THREE HOSTILE RE-READS, AND WHAT EACH ONE COST. This file has been adversarially re-checked three times, all on 2026-09-20. Every pass re-fetched the cited pages instead of re-reading the file, and every pass found FINER errors than the one before it — which is what convergence looks like, and also what a process looks like just before somebody declares victory early. PASS 1 re-fetched every source and hunted claims the cited page does not support. Across the batch of eight screen files it found 52 such claims, of which 6 were deleted and 41 narrowed; in THIS file six claims were corrected or narrowed and one causal clause was deleted along with the claim it rested on. The kinds, because the kind is the part that generalises: (1) AN UNDER-COUNT STATED AS FACT — 'ten tags across five colours' for the BedWars chat tags, where the page shows ten tags in SIX colours and the enumeration had silently dropped [PATRON] (#00ffff); (2) A TAG THAT IS NOT ON THE CITED PAGE — a [MOD] chat badge, where the page's moderator tags are [AC MOD] and [LEAD AC MOD] and MOD survives only as a blocked clan-tag stem; (3) THE SOURCE'S OWN SPECULATION RESTATED AS RECORDED CAUSE — the tablist's removal attributed to players disliking seeing others' kits, which the wiki hedges with 'most likely' in a Trivia line, and which two rules leaned on; (4) A DATE READ OFF A TRUNCATED VIEW — the LaunchData thread's 'last post 2025-11-03', which was only the last post the default .json stream returns. PASS 2 read the repaired file and found 64 further items across seven of the eight files, all graded minor. SEVEN of them were in this file. PASS 3 is this one, and it settled all seven: (1) AN ARITHMETIC ERROR INSIDE CORRECT DATA — the clan-chat outage was called 'roughly twenty months' while its own three dates, all correct against the wiki's History table, span 2022-05-21 to 2023-02-03, which is 258 days or about eight and a half months, an error of ~2.4x; (2) TWO CITED PAGES THAT DISAGREE, RECORDED AS ONE SETTLED FACT — ChannelTabsConfiguration.TextSize is 18 on chat-window.md and 14 on the class reference, both cited in the same row and both re-fetched; the file asserted 18 in the reference AND in the measurements limit above, so the same error sat in two places; the BOLDER half (BuilderSansBold vs BuilderSansMedium) is confirmed by both pages and was kept; (3) A QUANTIFIER DROPPED — 'commands are NOT case-sensitive' where the wiki says 'MOST of them are not case-sensitive'; (4) TWO CROSS-FILE CITATIONS THE CITED FILE DOES NOT SUPPORT — screen-shop.json was cited for reviewers misreading a tab row's selection states (it records a tab COLOUR objection, 'out of place being green') and for an authored-default-off convention (it records only that the shop's open button must live outside the shop frame); both were deleted and the deletions recorded where they stood; (5) A CLOSED LIST QUOTED FROM AN OPEN SOURCE — the ten reserved BedWars clan tags, whose wiki line ends 'Etc.'; (6) A TRUNCATION LESSON TAUGHT IN ONE ROW AND NOT APPLIED TO ITS SIBLINGS — two other DevForum rows were read through the same 20-post window and did not say so; both now declare their window; (7) A TITLE AND A FEATURE QUOTED INEXACTLY — the NovaChat topic's live title, and 'per-message custom sounds' for a line that reads 'Custom Sounds - Personalize notification sounds'. PASS 3 also found, unprompted, that THE FILE'S OWN SUMMARIES HAD STOPPED MATCHING IT: the provenance said six shipped games where five were read (nine wiki rows, five games), and two limits entries repeated the six. That is the same defect as a stale claim and is fixed above. WHAT IS STILL UNSETTLED, BY NAME, BECAUSE THIS IS THE LAST REPAIR ROUND: (a) THE CHANNEL-TAB TEXT SIZE. Roblox's guide and Roblox's class reference disagree, 18 against 14, and no amount of re-reading resolves it; it needs the property read in Studio, which nobody here has done. (b) THE TWO PARTIAL DEVFORUM WINDOWS. t/4513813 has ~325 unread replies and t/4644214 ~25; every claim drawn from them is from post 1 and posts 2–5, so neither row can be read as what the thread concluded. (c) THE BEDWARS RESERVED-TAG DENYLIST is longer than the ten examples the wiki publishes and the remainder is not discoverable from the page. (d) WHETHER THE LaunchData BUG IS FIXED is unknown, as the limit above says. (e) THE BLOX FRUITS LEADERBOARD contradicts itself (top 99 against 100) and is recorded as written rather than resolved. (f) NOTHING IN THIS FILE HAS BEEN CHECKED AGAINST A RUNNING GAME — all three passes compared text to text, and the wiki rows were read as wikitext with every embedded screenshot named and unseen. A FOURTH PASS WOULD FIND MORE. The honest reason to stop is not that the file is clean; it is that the remaining items are now smaller than the file's own measurement error, and a library that claims to be perfect is exactly the kind of claim this library exists to distrust. Nothing was invented to replace what was narrowed, and no claim was rescued with 'appears to' or 'suggests' — where a claim did not survive, it was deleted.
